work.title: The Pied Piper of Hamelin
work.note: The Pied Piper of Hamelin é um poema narrativo do inglês Robert Browning, publicado em 1842. Baseia-se numa lenda alemã: a cidade de Hamelin é invadida por ratos, e um flautista de roupa colorida promete livrá-la deles em troca de pagamento. facts.big: Do I have to…? · You don’t have to · You can’t
facts.label: Aula de dança
facts.sub: Pergunte Do I have to know the steps? Do I have to come with a partner? e What do I have to wear? Ouça You don’t have to. e You can’t take pictures.

facts.label: Aula de dança
facts.sub: Aulas de dança para iniciantes começam do zero. Ninguém precisa saber os passos antes, e o professor ensina com calma, passo a passo.

facts.label: Have to
facts.sub: Use have to para dizer o que é obrigatório e don’t have to para o que não é necessário. Use can’t para o que é proibido.

pages.title: One, two, three · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Friday evening in a warm dance studio in Miami. Mirrors cover one wall and music fills the room. Couples laugh and spin in the middle of the floor. Gui stands at the door with a small bag. He has never danced salsa before. A smiling instructor named Sofia waves at him.
“Welcome to salsa class! Are you ready to dance?” says Sofia. “I’m a little nervous. Do I have to know the steps?” says Gui. “No, you don’t have to. We start from zero.” says Sofia.

pages.title: One, two, three · 3/3
paragraphs: “Okay. Can I take pictures in class?” says Gui. “You can’t take pictures. Let’s focus and have fun!” says Sofia. Sofia teaches the basic step: one, two, three. Gui steps on his partner’s foot and says sorry. They laugh and try again, slower this time. After an hour, he can follow the rhythm. He drinks water and sweats with a big smile. Dancing begins with the courage to try.
